overview: This Senate resolution sets up a procedure for the Senate to consider 97 of the President's nominations together as a group, called 'en bloc,' rather than one at a time. The nominees include officials for the Departments of Labor, Homeland Security, Defense, Housing and Urban Development, the Treasury, and State, as well as ambassadors, U.S. attorneys, members of the National Labor Relations Board, judges for the District of Columbia's local Superior Court, and others. The resolution itself only makes it in order to bring the group up for a vote; the nominees still have to be confirmed. The Senate agreed to it by a vote of 52 to 47 on December 11, 2025.
for: Supporters say considering many nominees at once clears a long backlog and lets the government fill important positions without spending weeks of floor time on separate votes.
against: Critics say bundling nearly 100 nominees together reduces the Senate's ability to examine and vote on each person individually, weakening its role in reviewing presidential appointments.
